Subject: FintechCo — post-call recap & next steps (pricing / regional residency)

Thanks again for the call earlier today — good conversation and appreciate the level of detail on expected usage. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of ask / what we heard:
- Monthly token volume (generation + embeddings): ~50M–80M tokens/month, with peak bursts for batch reports.
- Target unit economics: FintechCo is thinking about a target of roughly $100 / 1M tokens (target ballpark).
- Primary constraints: EU data residency for production traffic; willing to consider US-hosted for non-sensitive workloads.
- Latency SLO: <300ms P95 for API calls; heavier batch jobs ok overnight.

Immediate pricing considerations (high-level):
- Hosted (US region): our standard hosted unit price for the requested profile is around $90 / 1M tokens.
- Hosted (EU region): typically ~20% premium due to EU region capacity and compliance footprint (~$108 / 1M tokens).
- Reserved/Dedicated: a 6–12mo commit can reduce unit cost ~20–35% depending on commit level and burst allowance.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): solves EU residency fully but has platform & infra fees; unit economics vary based on committed throughput.

Next steps I’m proposing:
1) I’ll send a simple pricing worksheet (attached) showing line items for US-hosted, EU-hosted, and Dedicated/reserved scenarios with your target volumes.
2) Alex/Priya — can you confirm expected steady-state tokens (low/high) and an initial budget range (monthly or annual)? That will let us model committed vs on-demand economics.
3) If the EU premium looks material, we can explore a hybrid approach: route sensitive traffic to EU-hosted or Private, and non-sensitive to US-hosted for cost savings.

Proposed follow-up: 30min on Friday to review the worksheet and surface any procurement/security questions.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sheet-20260303.xlsx, fintechco-mutual-action-plan-20260303.docx

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Expected steady-state: 60M tokens/month (with monthly variability roughly 50M–80M).
- Peak batch jobs: additional ~20–30M tokens processed overnight, not latency-sensitive.
- Budget: we’re aiming for a total first-year spend in the $60k–$90k range; that aligns with ~ $83–$125 / 1M tokens depending on region/commit.
- Residency: production transaction data must stay in the EU. We can route analytics and non-sensitive enrichment calls to US if needed, but product calls must be EU-resident.

Can you model two scenarios for the Friday call: (A) EU-hosted fully (on-demand and a 12mo reserved discount case) and (B) Hybrid (prod EU-hosted + non-prod US-hosted) showing net blended $/1M tokens and estimated monthly spend?

Appreciate it —
Alex
Director of Engineering
FintechCo

Alex — thanks for the clear numbers. I ran a quick model and attached the detailed worksheet (redwood-pricing-sheet-20260303.xlsx). High-level findings: 

Scenario A — EU-hosted (on-demand):
- Unit price: ~ $108 / 1M tokens
- For 60M tokens/mo -> ~$6,480/mo (~$77,760/yr) on on-demand pricing

Scenario A2 — EU-hosted (12mo reserved commit, 30% discount example):
- Unit price (reserved): ~ $75 / 1M tokens
- For 60M tokens/mo -> ~$4,500/mo (~$54,000/yr)

Scenario B — Hybrid (prod EU-hosted + non-prod US-hosted):
- Prod (EU) 40M tokens @ $108 = $4,320/mo
- Non-prod (US) 20M tokens @ $90 = $1,800/mo
- Blended = $6,120/mo (~$73,440/yr) -> blended ~$102 / 1M tokens

Notes / options:
- Dedicated / Reserved capacity: if FintechCo can commit to steady throughput, we can give deeper discounts and an SLA. Dedicated also simplifies data-residency for prod if you want VPC-only traffic.
- Private (on-prem / customer-managed): eliminates cross-region risks but introduces platform fees; we can provide an estimate if you want that comparison.

Requested for Friday call:
- Confirm which split to model for hybrid (prod/non-prod token split). I used 40/20 as a starter.
- Confirm appetite for a 12mo commit so I can show reserved-capacity pricing tiers.

I’ll want to include Marissa and Sean on the call to cover reserved capacity and procurement details — Marissa, Sean: are you available Friday 11am PT for a 30min sync with Alex/Priya?

Thanks,
Dylan
